1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with adequate line spacing in the cards, and codes use a legible monospace font.

2.why: Instructions are short sentence-case lines with no italics or dense paragraphs; the only all-caps text is the 'NORTHSTAR BANK' brand mark, not an instruction.

3.why: Content sits in a single narrow centered column with large fields and buttons that would fit a mobile viewport, though long log lines wrap awkwardly.

4.why: Each step carries one short instruction (e.g., 'Enter the delivered six-digit code.'), though terms like 'secret', 'authenticator' and the 'MFA' acronym are mildly technical.

5.why: Only the recovery-code field shows a format example ('ABCDE-FGHIJ'); the email, phone, verification-code and authenticator-code fields show no example input.

6.why: No screen contains more than two short sentences of instruction, and recovery codes are presented as a bulleted list rather than prose.

7.why: The secret and recovery codes are rendered as plain text with no dedicated copy button, so copying depends on the user manually selecting wrapped text.

8.why: No QR code or otpauth:// link appears on any screen; the authenticator step offers only a typed manual secret.

9.why: The fields look like standard inputs, but nothing visible in the screenshots confirms or denies browser autofill or password-manager support.

10.why: Every screen has a bold heading naming the step and one prominent blue primary button, though on the Authenticator screen the blue 'Confirm' outranks the gray 'Generate secret' that must be pressed first.

11.why: Sign-in and Verify screens ask one action, but the Authenticator screen combines generate-plus-enter and the 'MFA enabled' dashboard presents three competing buttons.

12.why: Most actions get plain confirmations ('Recovery code accepted. Remaining unused codes: 7.', 'Your authenticator is now enrolled.'), but what comes next is rarely stated and the failure case gives only 'We could not complete that request.'

13.why: Users can re-request codes via 'Regenerate recovery codes' (demonstrated) and retry sign-in after an error with entered values retained, with no visible penalty, though no reveal/hide toggle exists.

14.why: The only error message shown, 'We could not complete that request.', does not blame the user but states neither the problem nor how to fix it.

15.why: The authenticator step displays an explicit expiry ('Current test code: 130841 (expires at 19:55:30)'), imposing real time pressure on code entry even though reading itself is untimed.
